gaps: Which tool/action actually issues a cheque book request is not stated; the policy only names stop_cheque_payment and generic 'raise_request', so the final action (direct tool call vs. service request) is unclear
Which account the cheque book applies to (savings/current, linked product selection) and how to look it up or handle customers with multiple eligible accounts
Eligibility rules: account types allowed, minimum balance, KYC status, account status (dormant/frozen/closed), prior cheque book outstanding, which are only in the knowledge base and not specified
Number of leaves/cheque book variants (25/50/100, personalised vs. standard), and whether the customer must choose or a default applies
Fees/charges for the cheque book, whether they must be disclosed, and whether the customer must consent before debiting them
Delivery details: address on file vs. new address, branch pickup vs. courier, expected timelines, and whether address changes are in scope
Whether confirmation is required before submitting the request (policy lists confirmation only for specific irreversible actions, not cheque book requests)
Order of steps: when to search the knowledge base versus look up accounts versus submit the request, and what to do if KB hits are weak
Edge cases: customer asks for stop payment, lost/stolen cheque book, or cheque status in the same conversation; customer references an unlinked account (refuse)
Customer behavior: vague requests, changing their mind mid-flow, pushing for exceptions to ineligibility, or asking for escalation to a human
What to say on failure or ineligibility, and when to escalate/raise a service request versus decline
Bank-specific conventions such as the daily/annual request limits, the reference number or acknowledgment to give the customer, and what confirmation details to provide
